head.title: Supporting new/custom message types with MessageBuilder/Formatter

body.h1: Supporting new/custom message types with MessageBuilder/Formatter
body.p: Axis2 provides extended support for new or custom message types. This is done with using a extension point in the Axis2 architecture, called message builders and formatters. In Axis2 a builder is responsible of building the MessageContext by looking at the raw message transmitted and the formatter is responsible of the inverse of that, which is to serialize a MessageContext to the wire transfer format. Let's create a custom MessageBuilder/Formatter to add the support for a new message type.
Send your feedback or questions to: java-dev@axis.apache.org. ( Subscription details are available on the Axis2 site.) Kindly prefix subject with [Axis2].

body.h3: New ContentType handling with a custom message builder and formatter
body.p: Let's write a simple builder and formatter to add the support for a new content type
A builder implements org.apache.axis2.builder.Builder, which has a single method:
body.pre: public OMElement processDocument(InputStream inputStream, String contentType, MessageContext messageContext) throws AxisFault;
body.p: It reads the raw request from inputStream and returns the SOAP envelope (or the payload element) that the rest of the engine will process. The builders shipped with Axis2, for example org.apache.axis2.builder.ApplicationXMLBuilder and org.apache.axis2.builder.XFormURLEncodedBuilder, are good starting points.
writeTo serializes the outgoing message in the new format and getContentType returns the Content-Type header to send. See org.apache.axis2.kernel.http.ApplicationXMLFormatter for an example.
